objective: Review Filamajig NFC M4 codec registry, pinned PAXX U1 contract, exact preview, guarded NFC lifecycle, restart reconciliation, and verified one/two-tag persistence for correctness and release-blocking defects.
owner_requirements: Support Standard OpenSpool and PAXX U1 as explicit codec choices
Target exact PAXX firmware v1.5.2-paxx12-21 and do not claim generic compatibility
Show exactly which fields and JSON types are written or omitted and enforce NTAG215 capacity
Write one or two tags per physical spool and save bindings only after a fresh matching readback
Retain conservative unknown-write reconciliation without automatic rewrite across app restart
Validate on the Motorola Razr 2023 and require separate physical NTAG215 and U1 acceptance
change_summary: Added ordered TagCodecRegistry with stable IDs, compatibility targets, frozen write intents, exact included wire fields, and default PAXX selection
Routed preview and write arming through the selected codec; preview reports compatibility target, field names/types, omissions, JSON bytes, and total NDEF bytes against 492
Pinned PAXX to v1.5.2-paxx12-21 commit 8d97e83f and verified the retained parser SHA-256 against the exact tag checkout
Added byte-stable Standard/PAXX fixtures and supported type/subtype matrix tests; unknown fields and alpha remain losslessly read-only
Added transactional NFC-A binding slots one and two with codec ID, payload SHA-256, verification time, replacement/rebinding, and spool cascade
Persisted spool ID, codec ID, and tag position in write journal v3 so pending/unknown restart reconciliation can bind the correct tag only after verification
Added exact compatibility documentation and a real-device Android NDEF/capacity/round-trip acceptance test

objective_evidence.host: Protected full gate PASS: 98 tests, lint, app APK, and Android-test APK. Focused repository/journal tests PASS.
objective_evidence.device: Exact connected motorola razr 2023 on Android 16: both APKs installed; all five instrumentation tests PASS in 16.281 seconds. M4 payload is 286 JSON bytes and 308 total NDEF bytes against 492.
objective_evidence.paxx_source: Exact tag refs/tags/v1.5.2-paxx12-21 resolves to 8d97e83f0329b72c512563a8e98305cfbdef7a18; retained parser and exact checkout both hash e34cad67d090ea1978601f819ec89c27e0f4b0be56da0683ac6c279a8c7d2e40.
objective_evidence.physical: Not yet run. Current hardware acceptance requires owner presentation of NTAG215 tags to the 2023 Razr and the U1 running the pinned firmware. No physical success is claimed.

known_limits: Hardware recognition and radio reliability cannot be proven by unit or instrumentation tests and remain an explicit physical gate
The pinned PAXX parser ignores transmission_distance; the preview labels it as a Filamajig extension
Incoming alpha remains read-only because Filamajig does not yet offer lossless alpha editing
Catalog candidates can be written but must be saved locally before a physical-spool binding can be recorded
review_questions: Can a binding be recorded before semantic verification, against the wrong spool, wrong UID, wrong codec, or wrong tag position?
Can restart, null NDEF reads, callback errors, replacement, duplicate UID, or second-tag flows corrupt or falsely complete state?
Does the codec output exactly follow the pinned parser's field types, diameter conversion, color count, type/subtype behavior, and capacity limits?
Does the UI accurately distinguish Standard OpenSpool, pinned PAXX behavior, Filamajig extensions, omissions, and unbound catalog writes?
sanitization: No credentials, environment values, user database contents, NFC UIDs, device serials, network addresses, photos, or account data are included.
